tools.name: probe
tools.summary: Inspect a media file with ffprobe: duration, dimensions, codecs, streams.
tools.description: Inspect a media file with ffprobe: duration, dimensions, codecs, streams. The video block reports the coded size plus rotation (clockwise degrees from the display matrix or rotate tag, null when absent) and the display size — what a player actually shows, so a phone clip coded 1920x1080 with rotation 90 reports display 1080x1920. It also reports time_base, which concat --fast compares before stream-copying.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

tools.name: trim
tools.summary: Cut a clip out of a media file.
tools.description: Cut a clip out of a media file. Give start (seconds) plus duration OR end. Re-encodes by default for frame-accurate cuts; set stream_copy=true for fast lossless cuts (keyframe boundaries only). With stream_copy, set snap_to_keyframe=true to move start down / end up to the nearest keyframes so the cut lands exactly (see the keyframes tool first), or smart_cut=true to keep the exact start instead: only the head up to the next keyframe is re-encoded (source bitrate x1.2), the rest is stream-copied — exact start, near-lossless speed. Set snap_to_beat=true to move start down / end up to the nearest beats of the music instead (see the beat_grid tool first): the grid is measured from the audio, and the cut refuses when the grid is unreliable (speech, tone, drone — no steady beat to snap to). snap_to_beat works on re-encode cuts too, and refuses snap_to_keyframe and smart_cut. Set edge_buffer (0-1s, default 0) to widen the requested window by that much on both sides, clamped to the file edges — Outtake's 0.1s clip-edge buffer, so the cut never lands exactly on a word or action onset; the result reports requested_start/requested_end plus edge_buffer_applied (how much each side actually grew — less at the file edges). It composes with snap_to_keyframe/snap_to_beat (the buffer widens first, then the snap moves the buffered window) and refuses smart_cut (which lands the start exactly). Every video trim verifies the cut by default: check_frames compares 3 frames of the output (head/middle/tail) against the source at the requested times and reports cut_verified plus mean_abs_diff per frame (threshold max(5, normal_step)); a snap that moved the cut shows up as mismatched frames, but a buffer-only trim checks against the buffered start, so it verifies. Set check_frames=false to skip the verification. Set dry_run=true to print the exact ffmpeg command(s) that would run and write no file.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

output.description: Output file path

end.description: End time in seconds (alternative to duration)

stream_copy.description: Copy streams without re-encoding (fast, keyframe-accurate only)

snap_to_keyframe.description: With stream_copy only: snap start/end to the nearest keyframes (start down, end up)

snap_to_beat.description: Snap start/end to the nearest beats of the music (start down, end up; see beat_grid first). Works on re-encode cuts too; refuses snap_to_keyframe and smart_cut, and refuses when the measured beat grid is unreliable

snap_beat_method.description: Which beat grid snap_to_beat snaps to: grid (one steady tempo for the whole file) or dp (the DP tracker follows real onset peaks, so it stays on the beat when the tempo drifts — see beat_grid)

smart_cut.description: With stream_copy only: exact start by re-encoding only the head up to the next keyframe (source bitrate x1.2); refuses snap_to_keyframe

edge_buffer.description: Seconds of handle kept past each edge of the requested window (default 0): start moves earlier and end later by this much, clamped to the file edges — Outtake's 0.1s clip-edge buffer, so a cut never lands exactly on a word or action onset. Composes with snap_to_keyframe/snap_to_beat (buffer first, then snap); refuses smart_cut

check_frames.description: Verify the cut: compare 3 output frames against the source at the requested times (default true; false skips the check, audio-only inputs have nothing to check)

dry_run.description: Print the exact ffmpeg command(s) that would run (one for a plain cut, three for smart_cut: head re-encode, tail copy, concat) and write no file

tools.description: Build a contact sheet: N evenly spaced frames tiled into a grid image. tools.name: concat
tools.summary: Join 2+ media files into one.
tools.description: Join 2+ media files into one. By default it probes the clips first: identical clips (codec, size, fps, pixel format, time_base, audio) are stream-copied with no re-encoding (fast, lossless); differing clips are re-encoded so the join still works — except a time_base mismatch, a display-size mismatch, or any rotation difference, which go through the filter graph instead of the demuxer, because the demuxer copies timestamps verbatim and stretches the join (measured 10s+10s → 116.9s) and applies the first clip's display-matrix rotation to every clip (an upright second clip came out rotated 90 degrees and stretched). Size is compared on display dimensions (what the viewer sees after autorotate): a clip stored 1280x720 with rotation 90 displays 720x1280, and fast=true additionally needs identical stored dims + rotation. Set fast=true to require the stream-copy path (errors with the exact mismatch if clips differ), or fast=false to always re-encode. Set transition (e.g. fade, wipeleft, dissolve, circlecrop) to crossfade between clips instead of a hard cut — clips are normalized to the first clip's display size/fps first, and the output is sum(durations) minus (n-1) x transition_duration. Per-clip trim: give an input as {file, start, end} (seconds or MM:SS) — trims always re-encode with exact cuts, and fast=true refuses them (stream-copy cuts snap to keyframes). Set dry_run=true to print the exact ffmpeg command that would run and write no file (the demuxer path also returns list_file + list_content — write the content to that path first, then run the printed command as-is; the transition and trim paths print one exact filter-graph command; mode/expected_duration are computed from the probes, so they are exact; duration/size report null — measured on the real output).

start.description: Trim start in seconds or MM:SS (omit = clip start)

end.description: Trim end in seconds or MM:SS (omit = clip end)

inputs.description: Files in order; each may be a plain path or {file, start, end} to trim that clip

output.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

transition.description: xfade transition between clips: fade, fadeblack, wipeleft, wiperight, slideleft, dissolve, pixelize, circlecrop, ... (omit for a hard cut)

transition_duration.description: Transition length in seconds (must be shorter than the shortest clip)

fast.description: true = require stream-copy (error if clips differ), false = always re-encode, omit = auto-detect (copy when identical, re-encode otherwise)

dry_run.description: Print the exact ffmpeg command that would run and write no file (the demuxer path also returns list_file + list_content — write the content to that path first, then run the command as-is)

tools.description: Extract N evenly spaced frames as separate image files (frame-001.png, ...) into a directory, each with its timestamp — so you can actually look at what is in a video before cutting it. One frame per interval; timestamps are i * duration / count, and each frame is captured at its exact timestamp (two-stage seek), so the reported time is the frame's real time. sharpest=true picks the sharpest frame in each interval instead of the interval start (Laplacian mean, measured on disk; each entry reports sharpness and its window) — use it when a frame must be the cleanest one in its stretch, e.g. picking a cover frame out of a shaky pan.

tools.name: extract_frames
tools.summary: Export EVERY frame of a clip (or a time range) as a sequence of images (frame-0001.png, ...) into a directory — the full sequence, not N samples like frames.
tools.description: Export EVERY frame of a clip (or a time range) as a sequence of images (frame-0001.png, ...) into a directory — the full sequence, not N samples like frames. Use it to scrub a shot frame by frame: a fast move, a blink, a lip-sync slip that a 6-frame sample hides. fps defaults to the source frame rate (every frame); set it lower for a sparser sequence. Frame i lands at start + i/fps, and the count is verified on disk against round((end-start) * fps). PNG is written rgba (keeps alpha, e.g. ProRes 4444 sources). Refuses over 5000 frames — lower fps or shorten the range instead of filling the disk. Set dedup (0-10) to drop near-duplicate frames after extraction — one extra decode into 16x16 gray thumbs (siemd2/reel-relay's rule: a frame whose thumb differs from the last kept thumb by <= threshold is deleted); 2.0 is their summary default but collapses slow motion (measured: 8/20 of moving testsrc kept), so 0.5-1 only drops truly frozen frames. Set dry_run=true to print the exact ffmpeg command and write no file.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

output_dir.description: Directory to write the frame files into (created if needed)

fps.description: Frames per second to extract (default: the source frame rate, i.e. every frame)

start.description: Range start in seconds or MM:SS (default 0)

end.description: Range end in seconds or MM:SS (default the end of the file)

dedup.description: Near-duplicate removal threshold (mean abs diff on 16x16 gray thumbs, 0-255 scale; omit to keep every frame). 2.0 is reel-relay's summary default — it keeps 1/20 of a frozen clip but only 8/20 of steadily moving testsrc, so it collapses slow motion; 0.5-1 only drops truly frozen frames. tools.name: burn_captions
tools.summary: Burn subtitles into the video (hardcoded, always visible).
tools.description: Burn subtitles into the video (hardcoded, always visible). Accepts .srt, .ass or .vtt. Style: background (default — white text on a semi-transparent black box), outline (black outline, no box), shadow (thin outline + drop shadow), or glow (thick halo in the text's own colour, reads on bright footage). Defaults scale with frame height: ~60px type on 1080x1920, sitting ~500px above the bottom edge so platform UI (bottom ~480px) never covers the text. Explicit font_size / margin_v override. max_lines shrinks the type (measured with the same font libass draws, Liberation Sans) until every cue wraps to at most that many lines, never below a readability floor (1.6% of frame height, min 16px); a cue that still overflows at the floor burns at the floor and reports fit.fits=false. platform sets the default margin from that platform's own bottom UI depth (tiktok 520px at 1920 high, youtube 100px at 1080 high) and narrows the fit width to its text-safe rect; explicit margin_v wins. .ass files carry their own styles, so style, max_lines and the platform margin are ignored there (style_applied=false, fit=null with a note). Set dry_run=true to print the exact ffmpeg command and write no file (font_size/margin/style/fit are computed from the input, so they are exact; duration/size report null — measured on the real output).

tools.name: check
tools.summary: Verify a finished file against a platform delivery spec (tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube): dimensions, codecs, fps, duration limit, audio channels and measured…
tools.description: Verify a finished file against a platform delivery spec (tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube): dimensions, codecs, fps, duration limit, audio channels and measured loudness, plus a file-size limit where the platform has one. Video bitrate is checked as a warning only (platforms publish recommendations, not gates) and the result also reports the platform's text-safe zone. expected_duration fails the check when the measured duration is more than 0.5s off the brief (same tolerance as qa_report). audio_sync is always checked when both streams carry a duration: the video and audio stream lengths must agree within ±0.2s, or the file fails (a mux that pads or truncates one stream drifts captions and sync on some players); when either duration is missing the rule is skipped, not failed. With content=true, one extra decode pass scans for black frames, frozen frames, silence and audio peaks (0.1s windows above peak_threshold_db, default -1 dBFS; >= 0 dBFS is clipping) and folds them into the same pass/fail list with position-aware rules (a short black stretch at the very start/end is a warning — likely a fade — the same stretch mid-file fails). content_start/content_end (seconds) scan only that time range, reported on the file's own timeline. With baseline (a JSON file: a previous check --content result, a raw content result, or a plain {black, freeze, silence, peaks} span list — needs content=true), spans already in the baseline are reported as pre-existing and do not fail the gate, so only NEW spans fail: a render is judged on what it introduced, not on what the source already had (a detected interval counts as pre-existing when it overlaps a baseline span of the same kind by >= 50% of its own duration). With decoded_work=true, the decoded work is estimated from the probe (video pixel-frames + audio sample-channels) and warned when over the ceiling (250B pixel-frames / 6B sample-channels, plus per-stream limits: 3600s, 8192px, 120fps, 8ch, 192kHz) — a heavy input can OOM the machine before any tool reports progress. With palette (2-6 hex colors, e.g. "#DCC0A0,#A02D19,#1B2740") or palette_brand (amber-teal | warm-story | minimal-line, the same registry as assemble), frames are sampled at 2 fps and measured against the locked look: time-averaged share per color, off-palette share (pixels farther than 60 RGB from every palette color), mean luma, crushed/blown share and luma swing — crushed or blown past 2% fails, a mean luma outside 95-175 or more than half the pixels off-palette only warns. Policy tiers (idea: OpenEdit qc/policy.py): policy=full (default) runs every requested detector; light runs probe-based rules only and refuses content/baseline/palette (decode-heavy detectors are skipped, reported in `skipped` with complete:false — a light pass is not a full verification); skip runs nothing at all (no probe, no decode) and returns pass:true, complete:false with the skipped list — the stamp for a cache-hit proxy render. Env MEDIAKIT_QC_POLICY sets the default when policy is absent. With stamp=true it also writes a QC stamp sidecar <input>.mediakit-check.json (the verdict + the exact args + the media sha256/size + the ffmpeg/ffprobe versions, written atomically); with use_stamp=true it reuses the stamp instead of re-running the check when the media, the args and the toolchain all still match, and reports stamp.used=false with the stale reason (no_stamp/media_changed/args_mismatch/environment_mismatch/stamp_invalid) when they do not — a stamp never overrides a fresh run. stamp/use_stamp are refused under policy skip (a skip measures nothing, so there is nothing to stamp or reuse). Returns pass/fail per rule with fix hints. Run this before publishing.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

expected_duration.description: Expected duration in seconds (fail when the measured duration is more than 0.5s off)

content.description: Also scan content: black/frozen frames, silence and audio peaks; adds content_black/content_freeze/content_silence/content_peaks rules

content_start.description: Scan only from this time (seconds); needs content=true

content_end.description: Scan only up to this time (seconds); needs content=true

peak_threshold_db.description: Audio peak threshold in dBFS for the content_peaks rule (windows above it are reported; >= 0 dBFS is clipping; float audio can peak above 0)

baseline.description: Baseline JSON file (a previous check --content result, a raw content result, or a plain {black, freeze, silence, peaks} span list): spans it covers are reported as pre-existing and do not fail the gate — only NEW spans fail; needs content=true

faststart.description: Also check MP4 faststart (moov before mdat, measured by a pure-Node box walk) — fails when the file is not an MP4 or its moov box comes after mdat; re-mux with -movflags +faststart to fix

decoded_work.description: Also estimate the decoded work from the probe (video pixel-frames + audio sample-channels) and warn when it is over the ceiling (250B pixel-frames / 6B sample-channels, plus per-stream limits: 3600s, 8192px, 120fps, 8ch, 192kHz) — a heavy input can OOM the machine before any tool reports progress

palette.description: Locked look as 2-6 comma-separated hex colors, e.g. "#DCC0A0,#A02D19,#1B2740": frames are sampled at 2 fps and measured against it (time-averaged share per color, off-palette share, mean luma, crushed/blown share, luma swing) — crushed or blown past 2% fails; mutually exclusive with palette_brand

palette_brand.description: Locked look as a brand id (amber-teal | warm-story | minimal-line, same registry as assemble): the brand palette is measured instead of explicit colors; mutually exclusive with palette

policy.description: QC policy tier (idea: OpenEdit qc/policy.py): full (default) runs every requested detector; light runs probe-based rules only and refuses content/baseline/palette — decode-heavy detectors are skipped, reported in `skipped` with complete:false; skip runs nothing at all (no probe, no decode) and returns pass:true, complete:false with the skipped list. Env MEDIAKIT_QC_POLICY sets the default when absent

stamp.description: Write a QC stamp sidecar <input>.mediakit-check.json (the verdict + the exact args + the media sha256/size + the ffmpeg/ffprobe versions, written atomically); refused under policy skip (a skip measures nothing, so there is nothing to stamp)

tools.summary: Color-grade a video with a named preset (warm, cool, cinematic, noir, vintage) or one custom video filter chain (--filter).
tools.description: Color-grade a video with a named preset (warm, cool, cinematic, noir, vintage) or one custom video filter chain (--filter). Re-encodes video (libx264, crf 23 default), copies audio through untouched. The result reports the filter actually applied and the mean R/G/B of the middle frame before and after, measured on disk — so the grade is verified on pixels, not assumed from the filter string. Presets are fixed chains: warm pushes red and pulls blue, cool does the opposite, noir is black-and-white, vintage is faded and desaturated. Set dry_run=true to print the exact ffmpeg command and write no file (color_before is still measured on the input, read-only; color_after reports null — it is measured on the real output).

tools.name: make_loopable

tools.name: highlights
tools.summary: Find a clip's visual beats with perceptual hashes (EncodeX highlight.ts idea, re-implemented from the blockhash-js block-mean-value paper): sample frames at 2…
tools.description: Find a clip's visual beats with perceptual hashes (EncodeX highlight.ts idea, re-implemented from the blockhash-js block-mean-value paper): sample frames at 2 fps, hash each one as an 8x8 average hash (one bit per cell against the frame mean, +/-8 dead zone so encoder noise on a flat frame cannot flip bits, flat-frame tie-break mean > 127.5 -> 1), and call a frame a scene boundary when its hash jumps from the previous frame by >= threshold (normalized Hamming distance, default 0.15). A highlight is the span between two boundaries — spans shorter than min_span_seconds merge into a neighbour, so the timeline never shatters into slivers — and its score is the mean jump inside the span (how much the picture keeps changing there); top_highlights ranks them by score, then duration. Thumbnails are the greedy farthest-point frames (seed = biggest jump, then each pick maximizes its minimum Hamming distance to the picked set) — the most visually distinct moments, for a poster frame or a hook still. Probe-only, writes no file — also available as a probe-only batch operation and manifest step. Long files sample slower instead of refusing (frame cap 1200; below 0.5 fps the file is refused as too long).

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

fps.description: Sample rate in frames per second (0.5-5, default 2; long files sample slower automatically, down to 0.5)

threshold.description: Boundary threshold on the normalized Hamming jump 0-1 (default 0.15 — the EncodeX boundary; lower = more boundaries)

min_span_seconds.description: Spans shorter than this merge into a neighbour (0-30, default 2)

top.description: How many top highlights to rank (1-20, default 5)

thumbnail_count.description: How many farthest-point thumbnail candidates to return (0-10, default 3; 0 = none)

tools.summary: List the keyframe (I-frame) timestamps of a video (probe-only, writes no file), plus GOP min/max/avg interval.
tools.description: List the keyframe (I-frame) timestamps of a video (probe-only, writes no file), plus GOP min/max/avg interval. Check this before a stream-copy trim — cutting between keyframes silently shifts the cut. Pair with trim snap_to_keyframe=true to snap the cut onto keyframes. Set nearest (seconds) to also get the keyframe nearest one cut point: before (largest keyframe <= t), after (smallest >= t), closest, distance_seconds and direction (before/after/exact) — the snap target for a single cut without scanning the whole list.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

nearest.description: Time in seconds: also report the keyframe nearest this cut point (before/after/closest + distance). Must be within the clip

tools.name: audio_levels
tools.summary: Loudness curve + loudest moments of an audio stream (WyattBlue/auto-editor's `levels` idea: one value per timebase chunk, no threshold — the curve IS the data;…
tools.description: Loudness curve + loudest moments of an audio stream (WyattBlue/auto-editor's `levels` idea: one value per timebase chunk, no threshold — the curve IS the data; bariswha/losslesscut-mcp's audio_levels adds buckets + pickPeaks). One decode pass: per-frame astats Peak + RMS bucketed into bucket_seconds windows (default 1s), RMS averaged in the linear domain so each bucket's rms_db is the true energy mean. Returns every bucket {start, end, rms_db, peak_db} (a bucket of true digital silence reports nulls, never a fake -inf), a summary (max_peak_db, energy-mean mean_rms_db, min/max bucket RMS, dynamic_range_db, silent_buckets, loudest_bucket) and the top N peaks (default 5) ranked by peak_db and kept at least min_gap_seconds apart (default 2s — a 3s shout does not fill the whole list with its own neighbours; near-equal peaks tie at 0.1 dB and the earliest wins). The summary also carries `dynamics` (dziksu/synkinema's analyze_audio idea, same decode, no extra cost): quiet_p10_db / loud_p90_db as nearest-rank percentiles over the finite bucket RMS values, separation_db = p90 - p10 with a verdict (flat <6 dB, narrow <12, dynamic <24, wide beyond), and bed_fills_speech_gaps — gap buckets are true digital silence or >=20 dB below the loud p90, and the flag is true when those gaps still carry finite energy above -60 dBFS (a bed / room tone fills them) instead of digital silence; gap_bed_db is their energy-mean RMS. Probe-only, writes no file — also available as a probe-only batch operation and manifest step. Cap: at most 3600 buckets (raise bucket_seconds for long files).

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

bucket_seconds.description: Bucket width in seconds (0.1-60, default 1). At most 3600 buckets — a long file needs a wider bucket

top_n.description: How many loudest moments to return (0-50, default 5; 0 = curve only, no peaks)

min_gap_seconds.description: Minimum gap between two returned peaks in seconds (default 2; 0 keeps adjacent buckets)

tools.name: batch
tools.summary: Apply ONE operation to many files matching a glob under a folder, in one call: loudness, resize, reframe, compress, convert, extract_audio, reverse, rotate,…
tools.description: Apply ONE operation to many files matching a glob under a folder, in one call: loudness, resize, reframe, compress, convert, extract_audio, reverse, rotate, boomerang, make_loopable, freeze, grade, fit, trim, silence, chroma_key, cut_words, remove_retakes, smart_cut, clean_voice, slideshow, hook, bpm, beat_grid, tempo_drift, audio_levels, search_words, measure_pace or highlights — the same args for every file. Outputs are named <stem>-<operation>.<ext> under the output directory, mirroring the input tree. Returns one row per file (input order) with status ok/error/cached/skipped plus counts, so a failure in one file never hides the rest. Unchanged files are skipped via a content-hash cache (.mediakit-batch-cache.json in the output dir, verified against the output's size + sha256); jobs runs up to 8 files at once under one shared timeout_seconds budget; dry_run lists the planned outputs and writes nothing. cut_words, remove_retakes, smart_cut and search_words find each clip's words file by convention (<words_dir>/<stem>.words.json, default the input's own folder) — a clip with no words file fails its own row only. clean_voice writes .wav always (48 kHz mono float), whatever the input was, and a take whose plan needs clearvoice/sr fails its own row (pass steps without them to clean anyway). slideshow is the exception: a SET operation — the whole matched set of images (2-32) becomes ONE slideshow video (output_name, default slideshow.mp4) instead of one output per file, and the per-file cache does not apply. hook, bpm, beat_grid, tempo_drift, audio_levels, search_words, measure_pace and highlights are the probe-only exceptions: they write no file (output is null, output_suffix is null) — the measurement comes back in each row's result, and the cache stores that result instead of a file. Exit codes follow harken's scheme: the summary carries exit_code — 0 when every row is done/cached/skipped, 1 when any row failed — and the CLI exits with that code (2 for input errors: unknown operation, bad pattern/args, no matches), printing 'batch complete: X done, Y cached, Z skipped, W failed (of N)' to stderr. batch-manifest.jsonl streams one JSON line per finished row (completion order, index = the row's position in input order) as rows complete, so a batch killed mid-run still leaves a partial record; it is fresh-truncated each run so it always matches that run's batch-manifest.json.

operation.description: The operation to apply to every matched file

pattern.description: Glob matched against paths under input_dir: **/*.mp4 for every mp4 at any depth, sub/*.mp4 for one folder, or a bare *.mp4 (matches the basename at any depth)

input_dir.description: Folder to search under (recursive; hidden dirs, .git, node_modules and .next are skipped)

output_dir.description: Directory to write outputs + batch-manifest.json + batch-manifest.jsonl into (created if needed; files under it are never treated as inputs)

args.description: Operation arguments, same for every file (snake_case, e.g. {target_lufs: -14} for loudness, {preset: '720p'} for resize, {duration: 30, method: 'trim'} for fit). Unknown keys are refused, never silently ignored

jobs.description: Files processed at once (default 1 = sequential; capped at min(jobs, cpu count, 8))

output_suffix.description: Output filename suffix (default -<operation>). Empty string only with an output_dir different from the input dir

cache.description: Skip files whose input bytes + operation + args already produced the cached output (verified by output size + sha256)

stop_on_error.description: Stop starting new files after the first failure (in-flight files still finish; the rest are reported skipped)

timeout_seconds.description: Shared time budget for the whole batch in seconds (default 1800); files not started before it expires are reported skipped

max_files.description: Cap on matched files (extra matches are reported via truncated)

dry_run.description: List matched files + planned outputs without running anything or writing any file

tools.name: manifest
tools.summary: Run a whole edit pipeline from ONE declarative JSON manifest file: {version: 1, input, output, steps: [{tool, args}], qa?} — paths in the manifest are relative…
tools.description: Run a whole edit pipeline from ONE declarative JSON manifest file: {version: 1, input, output, steps: [{tool, args}], qa?} — paths in the manifest are relative to the manifest file. Steps run in order, each feeding the next (slideshow as step 1 only — it builds a video from images in args, so the manifest input should be the first slide image; download as step 1 only — it fetches from a URL in args, and when it is step 1 the manifest input may be omitted entirely; then trim, resize, reframe, compress, convert, extract_audio, reverse, rotate, boomerang, make_loopable, freeze, grade, fit, silence, denoise, interpolate, burn_captions, overlay, chroma_key, cut_words, remove_retakes, smart_cut; hook, bpm, beat_grid, tempo_drift, audio_levels, search_words, measure_pace and highlights are the probe-only steps — they analyze the chain file at that point and pass it through unchanged, so their results record WHY the next trim cuts where it does); the whole plan is validated before anything renders, so a typo fails in seconds. Each step is cached by content hash (input bytes + tool + args + sidecar-file bytes, verified against the cached output's size + sha256; a probe-only step stores only its result, there is no file to verify) — re-running an unchanged manifest re-encodes nothing, and editing step 3 only re-runs from step 3. Set qa to a platform (or 'any') to run qa_report on the final file. dry_run prints the plan and writes nothing — the approve-before-render gate. A step failure aborts the run and keeps the intermediates for inspection.

manifest_path.description: Path to the manifest JSON file

output.description: Output file path (overrides the manifest's output; the extension is adjusted to the step chain's final format when needed)

dry_run.description: Validate the manifest and list the planned steps without running anything or writing any file

cache.description: Skip steps whose input bytes + tool + args already produced the cached intermediate (verified by size + sha256)

keep_intermediates.description: Keep the per-step intermediate files under the output dir (deleted on success by default; always kept when a step fails)

tools.name: patch_manifest
tools.summary: Edit a manifest JSON file under a revision guard (AH64-dll/OpenEdit's revision-guard idea: a write against a stale revision is refused instead of silently…
tools.description: Edit a manifest JSON file under a revision guard (AH64-dll/OpenEdit's revision-guard idea: a write against a stale revision is refused instead of silently overwriting newer work). A manifest carries an optional top-level `revision` (absent = 0); the call requires `expected_revision` to match the file's current revision, applies 1-100 ops, proves the patched manifest still lints and plans (a real manifest --dry-run on a temp copy), then writes atomically (.partial + rename) with revision + 1 — and first copies the pre-patch bytes to `<manifest>.bak` (bariswha/losslesscut-mcp's set_segments idea), so .bak is always the revision just before the current one. A revision mismatch, a bad op, or a patched manifest that no longer validates all refuse with an error code (REVISION_MISMATCH / INVALID_ARG) and leave the file byte-identical — nothing is written. With dry_run (dziksu/synkinema's apply_operations dry_run + ChatCut's validateOnly: the approve-before-apply gate) the same guard + validation run, but nothing is written at all — no .bak, no revision bump — and the exact candidate document (with revision + 1, the bytes a real run would write) comes back in `candidate`, so the caller inspects it and re-issues the same call without dry_run to commit; a dry-run against a stale revision is still refused. Ops: set {path: input|output|qa|steps.N.tool|steps.N.args.KEY, value: scalar} (version/revision are managed, not settable); add_step {step: {tool, args?}, index?} (append, or insert at index); remove_step {index} (never the last step); replace_step {index, step: {tool, args?}}. Ops apply in order — each op addresses the step list as the previous ops left it (JSON Patch semantics). Returns revision_before/after, the backup path, a human-readable changes list, and the dry-run validation (steps + planned output).

manifest_path.description: Path to the manifest JSON file to patch

expected_revision.description: The revision the caller last read from the file (absent = 0). Must match the file's current revision or the call is refused with REVISION_MISMATCH and nothing is written

dry_run.description: Preview only: run the revision guard + op checks + manifest validation and return the exact candidate document (with revision + 1) in `candidate`, writing nothing — no .bak, no revision bump. Re-issue without dry_run to commit

patch.description: 1-100 patch operations, applied in order — each op addresses the list as the previous ops left it

tools.name: determinism
tools.summary: Check whether a linear pipeline manifest reproduces byte-identically (heristop/leclap's verify --rerender idea, for the manifest tool — assemble already has…
tools.description: Check whether a linear pipeline manifest reproduces byte-identically (heristop/leclap's verify --rerender idea, for the manifest tool — assemble already has verify --rerender; the manifest cache only verifies size + sha256 of an output it already stored, it never proves a fresh run reproduces the same bytes). Runs the same manifest N times (default 2, max 5) with the cache OFF — a cache hit would prove nothing — then compares byte sha256, decoded-frame digest (framemd5, moviepy's test pattern: compare decoded frames, never bytes), and measured properties (duration/frames/dimensions) across runs. Verdict byte_identical means the pipeline reproduces exactly (on this machine two identical libx264 encodes are byte-identical); content_identical means the frames match but container bytes differ, with the differing format tags named (usually creation_time); differs means the pipeline itself is nondeterministic, with the first differing run pair named. A download-first manifest re-fetches its URL on every run, unless the download step sets cache:true (then the verified per-URL cache serves it). keep_outputs keeps the per-run outputs under .mediakit-determinism-<pid> next to the manifest (removed by default).

manifest_path.description: Path to the manifest JSON file to re-run

runs.description: How many fresh renders to compare (2-5, default 2)

keep_outputs.description: Keep the per-run output files under .mediakit-determinism-<pid> next to the manifest (removed by default; always kept when a run fails)

tools.name: assemble
tools.summary: Film assembler (Autopilot-style): build a finished video from ONE declarative film manifest — shots on a voice-led timeline, mixed audio, burned captions, QA…
tools.description: Film assembler (Autopilot-style): build a finished video from ONE declarative film manifest — shots on a voice-led timeline, mixed audio, burned captions, QA and a receipt. The voice is the master clock: total = lead + measured voice duration + tail, and shot durations must cover that total EXACTLY in frames (no silent trim/pad/speed change). Modes: validate (no writes), plan (the director's storyboard disclosure: the resolved timeline — every shot with film-time start/end in seconds and frames, every transition with its blend offset, the voice/music/SFX audio timeline, chapters with ends — no writes and no approval; preview + approve are still required before render), preview (first N seconds at half size — show it to the user), approve (records the fingerprint of the previewed files; a human must have seen the preview), render (needs a matching approval, unless force:true). Shot segments are cached by content hash, so a re-render rebuilds only changed shots. v1: plain cuts, no per-shot text layers, one aspect per manifest. async:true (render only) returns a job_id immediately and renders in the background — poll the job tool. chapters [{title, at}] in the manifest become MP4 chapters in final.mp4. `preset` in the manifest (vertical/horizontal/square/cinematic/vertical-60) picks width/height/fps/style for the whole film; explicit fields win and are reported in preset_overrides, preset-filled fields in preset_applied. `brand` in the manifest (amber-teal/warm-story/minimal-line, see skills/shorts-video/brands.json — or your own ids from a MEDIAKIT_BRANDS file) paints the whole film in one channel look — palette fills template colors and text-layer color/size, its style fills the caption style when no preset or explicit style sets one; explicit values win and are reported in brand_overrides, brand-filled fields in brand_applied. NOT the manifest tool (that runs a linear edit pipeline). Shot roles (hook/context/core/payoff) and a film-level hook {shot, start?, end?} pin the opening segment — diagnose checks the arc (hook first, payoff last). A shot may carry variants — alternate takes A/B/C of the same kind, each with its own source fields and an optional hook label naming which hook it opens with — with selected (index or label, default 0) picking the one that renders; unselected takes are still probed, hashed and listed in the receipt, so switching the pick re-renders only that shot.

manifest_path.description: Path to the film manifest JSON file (see skills/shorts-video/references/assemble-manifest.md for the schema)

mode.description: validate: check the timeline math and files, write nothing. plan: the director's storyboard disclosure — the resolved timeline (every shot with film-time start/end, joins, the audio timeline, chapters with ends), write nothing, no approval. preview: render the first preview_seconds at half size. approve: record approval for the previewed files. render: full-resolution film (needs approval unless force).

output_dir.description: Output directory (required for preview/approve/render): preview.mp4 + preview.json, or final.mp4 + assemble-receipt.json

preview_seconds.description: Preview length in seconds (preview mode only, default 20)

force.description: Render without approval (render mode only; recorded as approval:'forced' in the receipt — use only when the user explicitly says so)

async.description: Render in the background (render mode only): validate + approval are checked now, then the call returns a job_id immediately and the render runs in a detached worker — poll the job tool for progress and the terminal result. Chapters [{title, at}] in the manifest become MP4 chapters in final.mp4.

tools.name: job
tools.summary: Inspect a durable async render job (started by assemble async:true): status shows progress (stage + percent) and the terminal result or error, plus…
tools.description: Inspect a durable async render job (started by assemble async:true): status shows progress (stage + percent) and the terminal result or error, plus estimate_remaining_seconds — a rough upper-bound ETA in whole seconds while the job runs (null when it is too early to tell, or the job is queued/terminal) — and estimate_basis naming how it was derived (progress-rate from the rate over the most recent 30s of the job's own percent history when that window holds at least 2 points, else the whole-run average rate, elapsed-progress from time since start, complete/not-started/terminal/too-early); treat the number as a rough guide, never a promise. list shows all jobs newest-first; cancel stops a queued or running job. Status also carries progress_history — every distinct percent the worker reported, so in-stage movement is provable without polling luck (list omits it). admission reports the render-job admission gate (max 2 active jobs / 10 starts per minute by default, env MEDIAKIT_MAX_JOBS / MEDIAKIT_MAX_JOB_STARTS_PER_MINUTE) — check it before starting a render so a refused start does not surprise you. Jobs live under MEDIAKIT_JOBS_DIR or <workdir>/.mediakit-jobs.

job_id.description: Job id (e.g. job-20261114-005800-a1b2c3d4) — required for status/cancel

action.description: status: read one job; list: all jobs; cancel: stop a queued/running job; admission: the job-start gate (no job_id needed)

tools.name: download
tools.summary: Download a media file from an http(s) URL into the workspace — stock footage, a reference clip, a music bed.
tools.description: Download a media file from an http(s) URL into the workspace — stock footage, a reference clip, a music bed. Typed and guarded: http/https only (no credentials in the URL), size cap enforced while streaming for direct files (default 500 MB, refused upfront when Content-Length already exceeds it), 5 redirects max, 300s timeout per attempt, written atomically via <output>.partial and renamed only on success, then probed — a file that is not media is deleted and reported, never left as a success. HLS (.m3u8) / DASH (.mpd) playlists are fetched with ffmpeg -c copy (re-mux, never re-encode) under a protocol whitelist, and the size cap is enforced after the fetch. The output extension is either given (must be a media extension) or derived from the Content-Type / URL path. Transient failures (HTTP 429/5xx, network errors) are retried with exponential backoff 1s/2s/4s honouring Retry-After (default 3 retries; timeouts and deterministic refusals are never retried). cache:true reuses a verified per-URL disk cache (size + sha256 checked, corrupt entries re-fetched; playlists are never cached). rate_limit_rps paces downloads in this process with a token bucket (0 = unlimited). License: pass license to declare the source's license (e.g. CC0, CC-BY, Public Domain — recorded in <output>.provenance.json, never guessed); a license policy file (MEDIAKIT_LICENSE_POLICY env, or license_policy_file per call: {allow?, deny?, require_license?}) gates the download BEFORE any fetch — a declared license outside the allow list, inside the deny list, or missing when required is refused with LICENSE_DENIED and costs zero bytes. Without a policy file the gate is off and the license is only recorded. Returns the output path, size, content-type, redirect count, attempts/retries, cache hit status, the declared license + policy verdict, and the probe summary (duration, dimensions, codecs).

url.description: http(s) URL of a direct media file (video/audio/image) or an HLS (.m3u8) / DASH (.mpd) playlist

output.description: Output file path — with a media extension, or without one (the extension is then derived from the Content-Type / URL path)

max_size_mb.description: Maximum download size in MB (default 500); refused upfront when Content-Length exceeds it, aborted mid-stream otherwise

timeout_seconds.description: Per-attempt timeout in seconds (default 300); each retry gets a fresh budget

cache.description: Reuse a verified per-URL disk cache (default off; lives under MEDIAKIT_DOWNLOAD_CACHE_DIR or ~/.cache/mediakit/downloads, keyed by URL, verified by size + sha256; playlists are never cached)

cache_dir.description: Cache directory override (default: MEDIAKIT_DOWNLOAD_CACHE_DIR env, else ~/.cache/mediakit/downloads)

max_retries.description: Retries for transient failures — HTTP 429/5xx and network errors (default 3; 0 = no retry; timeouts and deterministic refusals are never retried)

rate_limit_rps.description: Token-bucket rate limit in requests/second for this process (default 0 = unlimited; the bucket starts full, so a single download is never delayed)

license.description: License of the source as declared by the caller (e.g. CC0, CC-BY, Public Domain; aliases collapse to one spelling, anything else is kept verbatim) — recorded in the provenance file; with a license policy configured it is checked before any fetch, and a failing license is refused with LICENSE_DENIED

license_policy_file.description: Path to a license policy JSON file {allow?, deny?, require_license?} — overrides MEDIAKIT_LICENSE_POLICY for this call; without a policy file the gate is off and the license is only recorded

tools.name: audit
tools.summary: Read the audit log: every tool call this workspace has recorded (newest first), with its arguments hash, input/output files + SHA-256, duration and status.
tools.description: Read the audit log: every tool call this workspace has recorded (newest first), with its arguments hash, input/output files + SHA-256, duration and status. Filter by tool, status, or since a date; verify:true re-hashes the recorded files on disk and reports matched/missing/changed per file, so a stale or tampered output is caught instead of trusted.

limit.description: How many entries to return, newest first (default 20, max 200)

tool.description: Only entries for this tool name (e.g. trim, assemble)

since.description: Only entries at or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO timestamp)

verify.description: Re-hash every recorded file on disk and report matched/missing/changed per entry

tools.name: motion
tools.summary: Measure real movement in a video (probe-only, writes no file): per-second curve of the fraction of pixels that changed between adjacent frames, plus still…
tools.description: Measure real movement in a video (probe-only, writes no file): per-second curve of the fraction of pixels that changed between adjacent frames, plus still intervals and a verdict (moving / mostly-static / static). Use it as the director's motion gate — a shot that looks alive in the timeline but scores 0.0000 is a still wearing a video's clothes. A static title card measures 0.0000-0.0001, a bouncing ball 0.003-0.009, testsrc 0.06; the default still threshold 0.001 splits movement from encoder noise with a wide margin. Pass adaptive:true to calibrate the threshold to the clip instead: the threshold becomes min(max(threshold, p25-of-curve * adaptive_factor), max(adaptive_cap, threshold)) (defaults factor 2.0, cap 0.005), so light grain on a static shot (0.0007-0.0013) reads still while a bouncing ball (slowest second 0.007) still reads moving — the cap sits in the measured gap between grain and the slowest real motion. Pass lag_seconds to catch motion too slow for one frame step: the curve then compares frames N seconds apart (value at second k = change between second k and second k+N), so a 10s fade-in from black reads 0.00043 adjacent (static) but ~1.0 at lag 2. Still intervals in lag mode are corrected to clip time (end + lag, clamped to the duration); a still shorter than lag+1s, or one in the final lag seconds, is not reported — use lag 1 for short freezes.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

threshold.description: Still threshold on the moved-pixel fraction (0-0.5, default 0.001 = 0.1% of pixels; a window below it counts as still)

min_still_seconds.description: A still interval must last at least this long to be reported (default 2s; shorter still blips are ignored)

lag_seconds.description: Compare frames this many whole seconds apart instead of adjacent frames (default 0 = adjacent). Catches motion too slow for one frame step — a slow fade, a creeping zoom — at the cost of 1-second curve resolution; still intervals are corrected to clip time

adaptive.description: Calibrate the still threshold to this clip's own quiet quarter instead of using the fixed threshold (default false)

adaptive_factor.description: Adaptive mode: multiply the clip's 25th-percentile motion by this (default 2.0)

adaptive_cap.description: Adaptive mode: the calibrated threshold never exceeds this (default 0.005 — sits between light grain and the slowest real motion)

tools.name: hook
tools.summary: Find the best hook window in a clip (probe-only, writes no file): slide a window of duration seconds across the file and score each candidate on five measured…
tools.description: Find the best hook window in a clip (probe-only, writes no file): slide a window of duration seconds across the file and score each candidate on five measured signals — mean audio energy (astats RMS per frame, binned and normalized against the file's own loudest bin), speech coverage (silencedetect complement), scene cuts (a window opening on a cut, plus cuts inside it, reads as a new beat), real motion (per-frame pixel-diff fraction, binned on the same step grid, normalized against a fixed 0.06 reference — testsrc-level motion is 1.0 — with a 0.001 noise floor and a 0.005 file-level gate so a static clip never scores motion from encoder noise), and visual beats (the highlights perceptual-hash boundaries inside the window — 2+ beats is fully active, 1 beat is half; a boundary at the window start counts, the window opens on it). Score is 0.3*energy + 0.2*speech + 0.2*cut + 0.2*motion + 0.1*visual (audio 0.5 / video 0.5), fixed weights so two runs rank the same way; the top windows are greedy non-overlapping, so they are alternatives, not the same window shifted by one step. Returns the ranked candidates with the score breakdown (each carries visual + visual_beats), the highlight_boundaries, the per-step energy curve (each bin also carries motion + motion_fraction), pacing from real cuts (slow/medium/fast-cut), a trim object, and a suggested_trim command. The trim end snaps to the nearest quiet moment (shorts-maker-gpu's smart end point): within the last snap_window_seconds (default 5) the quietest bin — quiet is (energy + motion) / 2 — wins when it is at most half as busy as the window's own mean, earliest wins a tie so the cut lands where the quiet starts, and the snap never shortens the hook below max(4s, half the window); a uniformly loud window or a whole-file hook keeps its raw end (trim.snapped false + reason). Video-only input scores on cuts+motion; audio-only on energy+speech. Files over 20 minutes are refused (the astats log would exceed the capture buffer). Clip history: pass history_file (a JSON file {version: 1, records: [{source_sha256, start, end, score, recorded_at}]}) to check every candidate against moments already cut — a candidate is duplicate when it comes from the same source file (sha256) and overlaps a recorded window by >= history_overlap (default 0.5) of the shorter window, reported as duplicate + duplicate_of on the candidate; history reports records_checked/duplicates_found/recorded. With record: true the winning window is appended to the history file (atomic write, only the winner — the alternatives were never cut, so they stay eligible); record without history_file is refused. A missing history file is an empty history; a corrupt one fails loudly.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

duration.description: Hook window length in seconds, 4-20 (default 15 — the sonic-match 12-20s hook range)

top.description: How many ranked windows to return (default 3)

threshold_db.description: Silence threshold in dB for speech coverage (default -40)

history_file.description: JSON clip-history file to check candidates against (see description); a missing file is an empty history

record.description: Append the winning window to history_file after the run (needs history_file; only the winner is recorded)

history_overlap.description: Overlap fraction of the shorter window that marks a duplicate (default 0.5)

snap_window_seconds.description: How many seconds back from the window end to search for a quiet moment to snap the trim to (default 5)

snap_quiet.description: Snap the suggested trim end to the nearest quiet moment (default true; false keeps the raw window end)

tools.name: bpm
tools.summary: Measure the musical tempo of a clip in BPM (probe-only, writes no file): decode to mono PCM, build a spectral-flux onset function, find the period by…
tools.description: Measure the musical tempo of a clip in BPM (probe-only, writes no file): decode to mono PCM, build a spectral-flux onset function, find the period by autocorrelation + comb filterbank with a 120 BPM prior and an onset-recall tie-break (aubio tempo, re-implemented in pure Node). Returns bpm (1 decimal), beat_period_seconds, confidence 0-1, reliable flag, onset_recall, onsets_detected, first_beat_seconds and the first 16 beat times. A steady tone has no onsets and speech has no steady beat — both report reliable: false with low confidence instead of a confident wrong number; do not snap cuts to an unreliable grid. Files over 10 minutes or under 4s are refused.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

min_bpm.description: Lowest tempo to consider in BPM (default 40)

max_bpm.description: Highest tempo to consider in BPM (default 240)

tools.name: beat_grid
tools.summary: Return the full beat grid of a clip (probe-only, writes no file): the same spectral-flux + autocorrelation/comb measurement as bpm, expanded to every beat…
tools.description: Return the full beat grid of a clip (probe-only, writes no file): the same spectral-flux + autocorrelation/comb measurement as bpm, expanded to every beat across the file instead of the first 16. Returns bpm, beat_period_seconds, confidence, a reliable flag, onset_recall, onsets_detected, first_beat_seconds, beats (all of them, 3 decimals), beat_count and last_beat_seconds. A steady tone or speech reports reliable: false with a warning — do not snap cuts to an unreliable grid (trim snap_to_beat refuses it). The grid is rigid by default: one steady tempo for the whole file, so a clip whose tempo drifts will drift off it. Set method="dp" to run the DP beat tracker instead (librosa beat_track, re-implemented in pure Node): it picks real onset peaks near the grid, so the beats stay on the music while the tempo moves, and reports tempo_drift_seconds (worst distance from the rigid grid) and tempo_drift_cv (interval variation). Files over 10 minutes or under 4s are refused.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

min_bpm.description: Lowest tempo to consider in BPM (default 40)

max_bpm.description: Highest tempo to consider in BPM (default 240)

method.description: grid: one steady tempo + phase for the whole file (default); dp: DP beat tracker that follows real onset peaks, for takes whose tempo drifts

tools.name: tempo_drift
tools.summary: Measure the local tempo of a clip over time (probe-only, writes no file): sliding-window tempo estimation — the aubio pipeline (spectral-flux +…
tools.description: Measure the local tempo of a clip over time (probe-only, writes no file): sliding-window tempo estimation — the aubio pipeline (spectral-flux + autocorrelation/comb + 120 BPM prior + onset-recall tie-break) run on overlapping windows of the onset envelope, aggregated to a 1-second tempo_curve (the local-tempo idea of librosa's plp). Returns bpm (global), confidence, a reliable flag, tempo_curve (1s bins with bpm + confidence + reliable), start_bpm / end_bpm (median of the first/last 20% of reliable bins), delta_bpm, max_deviation_bpm, direction (speeding_up / slowing_down / steady) and verdict (steady / drifting / variable / unreliable). Use it before snapping cuts to a beat grid: a drifting take (120->132 over 12s reads delta +6.5) needs beat_grid --method dp, not the rigid grid. A steady tone or speech reports verdict unreliable. Files over 10 minutes or under 8s are refused.

input.description: Path to the file (relative or absolute)

min_bpm.description: Lowest tempo to consider in BPM (default 40)

max_bpm.description: Highest tempo to consider in BPM (default 240)

tools.name: verify
tools.summary: Verify an assemble render against its receipt (assemble-receipt.json from a full render): re-hash every input (manifest, voice, music, captions, sfx, shot…
tools.description: Verify an assemble render against its receipt (assemble-receipt.json from a full render): re-hash every input (manifest, voice, music, captions, sfx, shot assets) and the output file, re-measure duration/frames/dimensions/LUFS, and report matched/changed/missing per item with a pass/fail verdict and the first difference. With rerender:true, re-run assemble from the recorded manifest (force) into a temp directory and compare the new receipt against the old one — a byte-identical output plus matching inputs proves the render reproduces. Use it after any render you must trust (report videos, deliveries) and whenever a file has been edited since the render.

receipt.description: Path to assemble-receipt.json (written next to final.mp4 by a full assemble render)

rerender.description: Re-run assemble from the recorded manifest and compare the new receipt against the old one (default false = check the files on disk against the receipt only)

output_dir.description: Where the rerender goes (rerender mode only). Default: a temp directory next to the receipt, removed after the comparison — pass a directory to keep the rerendered film.

tools.name: verify_cuts
tools.summary: Verify an assemble render cuts where its film manifest promises: downscale the delivered video to a 270p draft, measure the real hard cuts with the content…
tools.description: Verify an assemble render cuts where its film manifest promises: downscale the delivered video to a 270p draft, measure the real hard cuts with the content scene detector, and compare them against the manifest's shot boundaries — a hard cut must land within tolerance (default 0.25s) of its promised time, a transition must show a real visual change across its blend window (measured as a frame diff, since a fade fires no scene cut), and any extra cut is reported as unexpected. Duration is checked against the voice timeline (±0.2s). Returns ok plus one entry per boundary (confirmed/missing/invisible_transition/unmeasured) and the list of unexpected cuts. Probe-only: writes nothing except a temp draft, removed afterwards unless keep_draft. With strips:true it also writes one 4-tile review strip per boundary (frames at cut-0.5/-0.1/+0.1/+0.5s, captured from the delivered video and labelled with offset + timestamp) into <video-stem>.cut-strips/ next to the video, or into strips_dir when given — the eye-check the numbers cannot give: open the strip and look at both sides of each seam.

manifest_path.description: Path to the film manifest JSON file (same schema as assemble)

video.description: Path to the rendered video to check (final.mp4 from a full assemble render)

tolerance.description: How far a measured cut may drift from its promised time, in seconds (default 0.25)

threshold.description: Content scene-detector threshold (default 0.05 — the calibrated content-detector default; raise it only if smooth animation inside a shot is reported as a cut)

draft_height.description: Draft height in px for the scene-detection pass (default 270 — detection is resolution-insensitive; raise it only if a cut is missed on the draft)

keep_draft.description: Keep the temp draft render and report its path (default false = removed afterwards)

strips.description: Also write one 4-tile review strip per boundary (frames at cut-0.5/-0.1/+0.1/+0.5s from the delivered video, labelled with offset + timestamp) — default false, the verify stays probe-only

strips_dir.description: Directory for the review strips (default <video-stem>.cut-strips/ next to the video; ignored unless strips is true)

tools.name: diagnose
tools.summary: Director preflight for an assemble film manifest: validate the manifest, then measure what validation cannot — real motion inside each video shot's exact window…
tools.description: Director preflight for an assemble film manifest: validate the manifest, then measure what validation cannot — real motion inside each video shot's exact window (a frozen video is an error), source geometry vs the film frame (upscale over 2x or a low fps warns), the visual seam across each transition (near-identical frames warn), voice loudness, caption coverage and gaps, music loop count, sfx tails past the film end, chapter alignment to cuts, text layers that are too tall or sit in the burned-caption band, and style pace (cuts per minute + longest hold scored against the style.json — an explicit style_file, or the style.json sitting next to the film; films under 15s are too short to compare), and per-shot pacing (a run of 3+ same-look shots, a shot under 1s or over 15s, dialogue denser than 15 chars/s). Probe-only, writes nothing. Returns a pass/warn/fail verdict with one check per finding and the first issue. A broken manifest returns verdict fail with format_error instead of throwing. With stamp=true it also writes a QC stamp sidecar <film>.mediakit-diagnose.json keyed on the film fingerprint (manifest + voice + music + sfx + captions + assets + brand) plus the style file hash and the ffmpeg/ffprobe versions; with use_stamp=true it reuses the stamp instead of re-running the preflight when the film, the style and the toolchain all still match, and reports stamp.used=false with the stale reason (no_stamp/film_changed/environment_mismatch/stamp_invalid) when they do not — a stamp never overrides a fresh run.

manifest_path.description: Path to the film manifest JSON file (same schema as assemble)

style_file.description: Style file to score the film's pace against (default: style.json next to the film manifest, when it exists)

stamp.description: Write a QC stamp sidecar <film>.mediakit-diagnose.json keyed on the film fingerprint + style file hash + toolchain versions (written atomically)

use_stamp.description: Reuse the QC stamp instead of re-running the preflight when the film, the style and the toolchain all still match; reports stamp.used=false with the stale reason when they do not

tools.name: align_voice
tools.summary: Align an assemble film's shot durations to its voice: split the voice across the shots that speak, in proportion to each shot's dialogue characters…
tools.description: Align an assemble film's shot durations to its voice: split the voice across the shots that speak, in proportion to each shot's dialogue characters (whitespace-free count, like agent-storyboard's estimateTiming), then snap each interior boundary to the middle of the nearest pause within snap_window_ms (default 600) so a cut never clips a word. Dialogue comes from each shot's `dialogue` field, overridden per shot by a --lines file [{shot, dialogue}]; shots with no dialogue keep their durations. Durations are whole frames at the film fps and each spoken run's frame sum is preserved, so the aligned film still tiles lead + voice + tail exactly. Plan mode (default) writes nothing and reports the dialogue_key (sha256 over [[shot id, dialogue]] in film order), per-shot durations/deltas/snap info, and violations (motion-gate, text layer past the new duration, transition too long, hook past the shot). Apply mode (--apply + --output) writes the aligned film — never over the input — embeds the dialogue it aligned from, re-validates the written file, and refuses when there are violations or when --expected-key differs from the computed key (dialogue changed or shots reordered — re-run without it to re-align).

film_path.description: Path to the assemble film manifest JSON file (same schema as assemble; each shot may carry a `dialogue` string)

lines_path.description: Optional JSON file [{shot, dialogue}] — overrides the film's `dialogue` field for the shots it names

threshold_db.description: Silence threshold in dBFS for pause detection (default -40, same as the silence tool)

min_silence_seconds.description: Shortest pause that counts as a snap target, in seconds (default 0.25 — shorter than the silence tool's 0.5, so natural speech pauses count)

snap_window_ms.description: Snap window in milliseconds: a pause midpoint within this far of the proportional boundary is used (default 600, agent-storyboard's window)

apply.description: Write the aligned film (needs output_path); without this, only the plan is returned and nothing is written

output_path.description: Where to write the aligned film JSON (required with apply=true; never the input film)

expected_key.description: Dialogue lock: refuse the apply unless the computed dialogue_key equals this value (dialogue changed or shots reordered)

tools.name: chapters
tools.summary: Generate chapter markers for a long talk or film from measured pauses, not guesses.
tools.description: Generate chapter markers for a long talk or film from measured pauses, not guesses. Two modes, exactly one: words_file (a transcribe --word-timestamps JSON) splits the transcript wherever the gap between two words reaches min_gap (default 2s) and titles each chapter from the first words spoken in it; input (a media file with audio) runs silencedetect and starts a chapter at each speech segment that follows a silence of at least min_gap, titled Part 1..N. The first chapter is always at 0 (YouTube requires the first chapter at 0:00) — when the first word/speech starts later the chapter is clamped to 0 and reported. Over max_chapters (default 32, the assemble cap) the closest neighbours merge first. Returns chapters in the assemble manifest shape {title, at}; pass output to also write that JSON to a file.

words_file.description: Transcript words JSON from transcribe --word-timestamps ({words:[{start,end,word}]}) — one of words_file / input

input.description: Media file with an audio stream — one of words_file / input; chapters start at speech after a silence

min_gap.description: Pause length in seconds that starts a new chapter (default 2)

title_words.description: Words taken from the start of each segment for its title (words mode only, default 4)

max_chapters.description: Chapter cap (default 32, the assemble cap); over it the closest neighbours merge first

threshold_db.description: Silence threshold in dBFS (input mode only, default -40)

min_duration.description: Shortest silence that counts, in seconds (input mode only, default 0.5)

output.description: Optional .json file to write {chapters:[{title, at}]} into (assemble manifest shape)

tools.name: transitions
tools.summary: List the xfade transition catalog (probe-only, writes no file): every transition name concat / slideshow / assemble accept, grouped by family — fade…
tools.description: List the xfade transition catalog (probe-only, writes no file): every transition name concat / slideshow / assemble accept, grouped by family — fade (cross-dissolve), wipe (hard edge sweep), slide (push off frame), smooth (eased slide), shape (geometric mask), diagonal, slice (strips peel away), wind (strips blow across), cover (curtain in), reveal (outgoing slides away), other (pixelize, radial, blur, zoom, squeeze). Returns total (58 on ffmpeg 8.1.2) plus per-category names and one-line descriptions. Pass category to narrow to one family; an unknown category is refused with the valid list.

category.description: One category name (fade, wipe, slide, smooth, shape, diagonal, slice, wind, cover, reveal, other) — omit for the full catalog

tools.name: export_timeline
tools.summary: Export an assemble film manifest to an OpenTimelineIO timeline (.otio) — the director's EDL for a real editor (DaVinci / Premiere / any OTIO adapter): the same…
tools.description: Export an assemble film manifest to an OpenTimelineIO timeline (.otio) — the director's EDL for a real editor (DaVinci / Premiere / any OTIO adapter): the same cuts, transitions, chapters and audio the ffmpeg render produces, with media linked by absolute file:// URL. One Video track (a Clip per image/video shot, a Gap per color/canvas_scene shot — generated frames have no file, so the gap is honest — with a Transition between joined shots), plus Audio tracks for Voice (lead gap + voice + tail gap), Music (looped to the film length) and SFX (each at its timestamp). Chapters become Marker.2 markers on the video track (OTIO 0.18 cannot read Marker.1). Transitions map the xfade join exactly: in_offset/out_offset are the split of the transition frames (in = ceil half, out = floor half), so the OTIO dissolve starts where the ffmpeg blend starts; fade-family xfade names become SMPTE_Dissolve, the rest Custom_Transition with the xfade name in metadata. Frame math is rational, never float seconds: every boundary is a whole number of frames at the film fps, and frame_math reports the snap error per shot (a 26.575s shot at 30fps is 797 frames with a -0.25-frame snap, never 797.25 frames). A file that passed validation and then vanished is linked with available_range null and listed in media.missing instead of failing the export. The writer self-checks the document (every track sums to exactly total_frames) and refuses to write a bad one. Returns the timeline summary, frame_math, media.missing, warnings and the self-check.

manifest_path.description: Path to the assemble film manifest (film.json) to export

output.description: Output .otio path (must end in .otio)

tools.name: safety
tools.summary: Safety tiers for every MediaKit tool (EncodeX's safety-tier idea): READ tools only probe and write nothing (probe, check, hook, diagnose); PLAN tools answer a…
tools.description: Safety tiers for every MediaKit tool (EncodeX's safety-tier idea): READ tools only probe and write nothing (probe, check, hook, diagnose); PLAN tools answer a question by transient work and leave no artifact (determinism renders to a hidden work dir that is removed, verify_cuts renders a draft to temp — plus caller-requested review strips when strips:true, estimate_conversion sample-encodes to temp, job only reads/cancels job state); WRITE tools produce a file the caller asked for and never overwrite their own input (prepareOutput refuses that); DESTRUCTIVE tools replace or remove a user artifact in place — only patch_manifest, and it is guarded by expected_revision plus a .bak backup. Returns the tier table with every tool named, the counts, and the rules. Read this before letting an agent loose on a workspace.

tools.name: estimate_conversion
tools.summary: Estimate a convert's output size and time BEFORE running it (EncodeX's estimate_conversion idea): measured, not a bitrate table.
tools.description: Estimate a convert's output size and time BEFORE running it (EncodeX's estimate_conversion idea): measured, not a bitrate table. At 2 window positions (25%/75% of the file) it encodes the same start twice, video-only, at a short length (default 2s) and a long length (default 6s) with accurate seek — both start with one keyframe, so steady_rate = (long_bytes - short_bytes) / (long - short) and iframe_bytes = short_bytes - steady_rate x short; full video = steady_rate x duration + iframe_bytes x one keyframe per 250 frames (the x264/x265 default GOP). Audio is copied by default (the convert default), so its cost is the probed source audio bitrate x duration; pass audio_bitrate_kbps to re-encode audio, measured from one audio-only sample encode. Time is a rough ETA (duration / measured encode speed + one measured startup); size is the precise part — on the fixtures it lands within 10% (hook-source -6.1%, source +4.2% at crf 23; source.mp4 takes the full-encode path and is exact). A file shorter than the sample budget is encoded whole, so the answer is exact instead of estimated. Leaves no artifact: samples go to a temp dir that is removed afterwards. Only libx264/libx265 (vp9/av1 use different quality knobs, so a crf estimate would not match convert).

audio_bitrate_kbps.description: Re-encode audio to this bitrate in kbps; omit to copy the source audio (the convert default)

tools.description: Release checkpoint — one QC gate for a finished clip (KyaniteLabs/kinocut's release-checkpoint idea): verify against the assemble receipt (pass only when 0 changed/missing, and the receipt must be for this input), the platform check (default tiktok), full loudness (pass |LUFS+14| <= 1.0 and true peak <= -1.0 dBTP, warn |LUFS+14| <= 2.0 and TP <= -0.5), clipping (fail on any peak >= 0 dBFS), cut positions against the film manifest (fail on any missing boundary or unexpected cut), plus a contact sheet at the inspection points — shot midpoints + transition midpoints from the manifest, evenly spaced without one. Run it on every deliverable before calling it done.
